 ORDER

This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the order dated 07.08.2023 passed in Spl. (P) No.24/2022 by the Additional Sessions Judge, FTSC-1 (Spl.
POCSO) Court, Kalaburagi, on the application filed by the petitioner under Section 311 of Cr.P.C.
whereby the trial Court dismissed the application filed by the petitioner for recalling P.Ws.1 to 3 and 12 to 15.
2.

Additional Sessions Judge, FTSC-1 (Spl.
POCSO) Court, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent State.
3. The case of the petitioner-accused is that he is facing trial for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act and the matter was under trial.
The prosecution examined 15 witnesses.

The learned counsel for the petitioner-accused did not cross examine P.Ws.12 to 15 and P.Ws.1 to 3 required to be recalled for the purpose of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8656 confronting some love letters written by P.W.1.
There was video C.D. produced by the investigation officer to the Court, which is also not cross examined by the learned counsel for the accused in the cross examination of P.Ws.1 to 3.
Therefore, the petitioner-accused filed an application for recalling the said witnesses, which came to be dismissed.

Hence, the petitioner is before this Court.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that during the deposition of P.Ws.12 to 15, the learned counsel appeared for the petitioner-accused No.1 was remained absent and hence, the trial Court taken the cross examination by learned counsel for accused No.1 as 'nil'.
Like wise, P.Ws.1. to 3 have been cross examined by learned counsel for accused.
However, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there was love affairs between the complainant i.e. victim and the petitioner - accused No.1.

There are some love letters that were not confronted by the earlier counsel and there was statement recorded by the Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., which was opened in the open Court while examination and a copy was given and not able to cross examine P.W.1.

No NC:
2023:KHC-K:8656 proper affidavit is given.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the application.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader objected the petition mainly on the ground that there is a bar under Section 33(5) of POCSO Act for recalling the witness frequently.

Hence,
prayed for dismissing the petition.

2 6.

Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, perused the records, especially the evidence of P.Ws.12 to 15 where the trial Court has taken the cross examination by accused No.1 as the learned counsel was absent.
The trial Court insisted accused NO.1 to put questions, but he was not able to put the questions.
Therefore, the cross examination of accused No.1 was taken as nil.
However, P.Ws.1 to 3 have been cross examined by accused No.1, some important questions were left out.
It is alleged that some love letters also left out and these have to be confronted.

Therefore,
though there is a bar under Section 33(5) of the POCSO Act that the victim shall not be frequently called for the purpose of testifying before the Court and the victim was aged NC: 2023:KHC-K:8656 15 years at the time of examination in the year 2022, non examination of cross examination of P.Ws.12 to 15 will definitely prejudice the case of accused in the trial.

7. This Court in the catena of decisions has held that merely there was restriction in recalling the witness under Section 33(5) of the POCSO Act, the fair trial cannot be denied which is guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Such being the case, rejection the application by the trial Court is not correct and is liable to be set aside.

8. However, P.Ws.2 and 3 are the parents of the victim, they are only the circumstantial and hearsay witnesses to the incident but the victim is the only material witness to the offence under POCSO and rape case.
Such being the case, recalling P.Ws.2 and 3 is not necessary.

However, P.W.1 is necessary for learned counsel for accused to elicit some of the evidence from this witnesses either by way of confronting the documents or further cross examination in respect of Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as the same was supplied only on the day of recording the evidence.
Therefore, a fair trial to the accused be NC: 2023:KHC-K:8656 given as the offence is under POCSO Act and the punishment provided under the said Act is 20 years and fine.
9. Such being the case, it is necessary for the Court to give an opportunity to the petitioner-accused to further cross examine P.W. No.1 and to cross examine P.Ws.12 to 15.
Therefore, rejecting the application by the trial Court is not correct.
Hence, the order of the trial court is set aside.

10. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
 (i) The petition is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned order of the trial Court is set aside and modified.
(iii) The petitioner is permitted to recall P.W.1-victim for the purpose of further cross examination and cross examination of P.W.12 to 15.

(iv) Cost of Rs.2000/- shall be payable to P.W.1 and Rs.3000/- to P.W.15 who comes from Hyderabad.
